Direction: A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to “No improvement”.

The behaviour of my father with all his subordinates is so pleasing that everyone come forward to help him.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Comes forward​'.

Key Points​

  • The use of 'Come forward' is inappropriate for the given sentence.
  • 'Everyone' is an indefinite pronoun which always requires a singular verb.
  • Example:
    • Everyone have done his or her homework. [Incorrect]
    • Everyone has done his or her homework. [Correct]
  • Hence, the underlined part of the sentence should be replaced by 'Comes forward'.
     

​Correct sentence: The behaviour of my father with all his subordinates is so pleasing that everyone comes forward to help him.

Additional Information

  • The indefinite pronouns like anyone, everyone, someone, no one, nobody are always singular and, therefore, require singular verbs.
  • Some indefinite pronouns — such as all, some — are singular or plural depending on what they're referring to.
  • Examples:
    • Some of the beads are missing.
    • Some of the water is gone.

Direction: A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to “No improvement”.

The car broke up in the middle of the dense forest.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Broke down.

Key Points​

  • The use of 'Broke up' is inappropriate for the given sentence.
  • Broke down is a phrasal verb which means stopped working properly.
  • Example:
    • The bus broke down due to less maintenance.
  • ​Hence, the underlined part of the sentence should be replaced by 'Broke down'.
     

​Correct sentence: The car broke down in the middle of the dense forest.

Additional Information

  • 'Broke in' is a phrasal verb which means wore or used something new until it is comfortable.
    • Example:
      • He needed to broke those shoes in before he went hiking.
  • ​​'Broke' is a verb which means separated or caused to separate into pieces as a result of a blow, shock, or strain.
    • Example:
      • The branch broke with a loud snap.
  • ​'​Broke over' is a phrasal verb which means crashed into something and fell apart or shattered.
    • Example:
      • The wave broke over the rocks of the jetty.

questions.text:
Direction: A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to “No improvement”.

I will not attend the reception until I am asked to.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Unless.

Key Points​

  • The use of 'Until' is inappropriate for the given sentence.
  • Let us look at the meaning of the word "Unless and Until":
    • Unless: except if (used to introduce the case in which a statement being made is not true or valid).
    • Until: up to the point in time
  • Example:
    • Unless you have a photographic memory, repetition is vital.​
  • Hence, the underlined phrase should be replaced by 'Unless'.
     

​Correct sentence: I will not attend the reception unless I am asked to.

Additional Information

  • Though means despite the fact that; although.
    • Example:
      • Though they were speaking in undertones, Percival could hear them.
  • ​​Even means equal in number, amount, or value.
    • Except: not including; but not.
  • ​​Except means not including, but not.
    • Example:
      • They work every day except Sunday.

It is advisable that we should never impose to much work on anyone.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Too much.

Key Points​

  • The meaning of the phrase 'Too much' is an intolerable, impossible, or exhausting situation or experience.
  • Example:
    • The effort proved too much for her.
  • Hence, the underlined phrase should be replaced by 'Too much'.
     

​Correct sentence: It is advisable that we should never impose too much work on anyone.

Additional Information

  • 'Such' can be used as a determiner, predeterminer and pronoun which means of the type previously mentioned.
    • Example:
      • I have been involved in many such courses.
  • ​​'Very much' is an idiom which means to a very great degree or extent.
    • Example:
      • We enjoyed ourselves very much.
  • ​​'A lot' means many or to a great extent.
    • Example:
      • Mona reads a lot of books during her morning hours.

Direction: A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to “No improvement”.

She was advised by him to listening to her doctor.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Listen to.

Key Points ​

  • The use of the phrasal verb 'Listening to' is inappropriate for the given sentence.
  • 'Listen' always takes the preposition 'to' after it. 
    • Example:
      • I listen to music.
  • 'Hear' is not used with 'to'
    • Example:
      • I didn't hear what she said.​
  • Hence, the underlined phrase should be replaced by 'Listen to'.
     

​Correct sentence: She was advised by him to listen to her doctor.

Additional Information

  • 'Verbs' are words that show action (sing), occurrence (develop), or state of being (exist).
    • Almost every sentence requires a verb.
    • The basic form of a verb is known as its infinitive.
    • The forms call, love, break, and go are all infinitives.
  • Example:
    • I want to play.
    • We all were sleeping that day.

questions.text: According to the Prime Minister, what is dangerous and harmful to the development of the country?

options.text: The hindrance in the distribution of freebies.
The interference of Finance Commission in the distribution of freebies.
The less involvement of youth in distributing and accepting freebies.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'The distribution of freebies.'

Key Points

  • The given passage is all about the concern over ‘freebies’ in Indian politics.
  • The last sentence of the first paragraph says "He hit out at the Opposition parties for offering freebies and said that this was dangerous and harmful to the development of the country".
  • From the above sentences, we can say that according to the Prime Minister, the distribution of freebies is dangerous and harmful to the development of the country.
     

Hence, the only possible answer is option 2.

Important Points

  • ​Given below are the points, we should keep in mind while solving questions of reading comprehension-
    • Identify the purpose of reading. Try to go through the question first and then the passage so that you can just focus on the things you need to look at in the passage.
    • Anticipate what may lie ahead. Look out for specific information in the passage.

questions.text:
Which of the following is/are incorrect according to the given passage?

A. Mr. Narendra Modi warned the youth not to get carried away by freebies.

B. The Court has suggested the Finance Commission to stay out of the matter of the 'freebies' issue.

C. The Chief Justice of India remarked ‘freebies’ as an unimportant issue.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Both B and C.'

Key Points

  • The second sentence of the first paragraph says "Speaking at the inaugural ceremony of the Bundelkhand Expressway (Uttar Pradesh) on July 16, Prime Minister Narendra Modi warned youth not to get carried away by the ‘revari culture’, where votes are sought by promising ‘freebies’.''
    • From the above sentence, we can say that statement A is correct according to the given passage.​​​
  • The last sentence of the second paragraph says "The Court also suggested that the Finance Commission could be involved to look into the matter and propose solutions'' and the second sentence of the second paragraph says "It has been reported that during the hearing, the Chief Justice of India remarked that ‘freebies’ were a serious issue and asked the Central government to take a stand on the need to control the announcement of ‘freebies’ by political parties during election campaigns''.
    • From the above sentence, we can say that statements B and C are incorrect according to the given passage.​
       

Hence, the only possible answer is option 4.

questions.text: What is the central theme of the passage?

options.text: Concern over fewer ‘freebies’ in Indian politics.
Concern over banning ‘freebies’ in Indian politics.
Concern over the unequal distribution of ‘freebies’.
The Supreme Court allowing ‘freebies’ in Indian politics.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is '​​Concern over ‘freebies’ in Indian politics.'

Key Points

  • The first sentence of the first paragraph says ''Concern over ‘freebies’ in Indian politics has recently been expressed by those in the highest offices in the country'', the last sentence of the first paragraph says ''He hit out at the Opposition parties for offering freebies and said that this was dangerous and harmful to the development of the country'' and the second sentence of the second paragraph concludes ''It has been reported that during the hearing, the Chief Justice of India remarked that ‘freebies’ were a serious issue and asked the Central government to take a stand on the need to control the announcement of ‘freebies’ by political parties during election campaigns''.
  • From the above sentences, we can say that the central theme of the passage is ''​​​Concern over ‘freebies’ in Indian politics.''
    ​

Hence, the only possible answer is option 3.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of the word 'Distort'.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Accurate.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Distort' means To give a misleading or false account or impression of something.
    • Example: They said that it had printed false information to distort the facts.
  • Let's look at the meaning of the given options:-
    • Accurate​ - Correct in all details; exact.
      • Example: She gave an accurate account of the case.
    • Pervert - To distort or corrupt the original course, meaning, or state of something.
      • Example: He was charged with conspiring to pervert the course of justice.
    • Garble - To reproduce something in a confused and distorted way.
      • Example: You garble my words from their real meaning.
    • Prejudice - Preconceived opinion that is not based on reason or actual experience.
      • Example: The party's policies were based on prejudice rather than on any coherent ideology.
    • Misrepresent - To give a false or misleading account of the nature of something.
      • Example: These statistics grossly misrepresent the reality.
         

Hence, the only possible answer is option 1.

Additional Information

  • The antonyms of the word 'Distort' are "Accurate, Interpret, Decipher".
  • The synonyms of the word 'Distort' are "Pervert​, Garble, Misrepresent".

questions.text: Choose the synonym of the word 'Irrational'.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Fallacious.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Irrational' means Not logical or reasonable.
    • Example: She has an irrational dread of hospitals.
  • Let's look at the meaning of the given options:-
    • Logical - Characterized by or capable of clear, sound reasoning.
      • Example: Students need the ability to construct a logical argument.
    • Reasonable - Having sound judgment; fair and sensible.
      • Example: It seems a perfectly reasonable request to make.
    • Sound - Based on valid reason or good judgement.
      • Example: She gave me some very sound advice.
    • Valid - Having a sound basis in logic or fact; reasonable or cogent.
      • Example: Accepting valid criticism is also part of this group of assertive actions.
    • Fallacious - Based on a false idea; illogical.
      • Example: His argument is based on fallacious reasoning.
         

Hence, the only possible answer is option 5.

Additional Information

  • The synonyms of the word 'Irrational' are "Fallacious, Illogical, Invalid".
  • The antonyms of the word 'Irrational' are "Logical, Reasonable, Valid".

questions.text:
In the following question, two columns are given containing three phrases each. In the first column, phrases are A, B, and C, and in the second column, the phrases are D, E and F. A phrase from the first column may or may not connect with a phrase from the second column to make a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. There are five options, four of which display the sequence(s) in which the phrases can be joined to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. If, none of the options given forms a correct sentence after combination, select ‘None of these’ as your answer.  

Column (1)

Column (2)

(A) The trend continues to this day and has spread to 

(D) respect for the whole community.

(B) Our love for the country should be conditioned by

(E) our duties and responsibilities towards that family.

(C) We are the members of a large human family and so cannot neglect 

(F) recently industrialized portions of the world.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e., A-F, B-D and C-E.

Key PointsWe need to join the sentence segments in column 1 with those in column 2 to create sentences that are conceptually and grammatically correct. Let us see how the sentence parts can join.

  • Part A talks about the spread of a certain trend, so conceptually, it should join with the part that explains where the trend has spread to. So, A-F. 
  • Part B talks about a conditioning and the use of the preposition 'by' means it should be followed by the part that acts as the agent of this 'conditioning'. Between, parts D and E, part D is a better fit (part E talks about 'family' which is not relevant here). So, B-D.
  • Part C talks about 'we' being a part of a family and how 'we' cannot neglect something. Part E best mentions what 'we' cannot neglect. So, C-D.
     

In the given options, all three joined sentences are reflected in option 3, making it the correct answer.

In the following question, two columns are given containing three phrases each. In the first column, phrases are A, B, and C, and in the second column, the phrases are D, E and F. A phrase from the first column may or may not connect with a phrase from the second column to make a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. There are five options, four of which display the sequence(s) in which the phrases can be joined to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. If, none of the options given forms a correct sentence after combination, select ‘None of these’ as your answer.  

Column (1)

Column (2)

(A) There are books and books but 

(D) most of the rainfall received in India and some other parts of the world.

(B) Narrow prejudice can do nothing 

(E) to bring misfortune.

(C) The monsoon, which is essentially the seasonal reversal in wind direction, causes 

(F) our hours of reading are very few.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e., A-F and C-D.

Key PointsWe need to join the sentence segments in column 1 with those in column 2 to create sentences that are conceptually and grammatically correct. Let us see how the sentence parts can join.

  • Part A talks about books and ends with the coordinating conjunction 'but'. Contextually, it best joins with part F as it deals with 'reading'. Grammatically, this joining is correct as 'but' joins two clauses that are equal in importance but contrast with each other. So, A-F.
  • Part B states how prejudice brings nothing. It cannot be joined with part D as it talks about rainfall. Joining it to part E is also grammatically and contextually incorrect. So, part B and part E are incomplete sentence segments.
  • Part C talks about monsoon and how it causes something. The effect it causes is mentioned in part D. So, C-D.
     

In the given options, only A-F and C-D are reflected in option 1, making it the correct answer.

In the following question, two columns are given containing three phrases each. In the first column, phrases are A, B, and C, and in the second column, the phrases are D, E and F. A phrase from the first column may or may not connect with a phrase from the second column to make a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. There are five options, four of which display the sequence(s) in which the phrases can be joined to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. If, none of the options given forms a correct sentence after combination, select ‘None of these’ as your answer.  
 

Column (1)

Column (2)

(A) Prior to the nineteenth century, both human and animal populations were

(B) Early biologists tried to explain the transition to smaller

questions.text:
Given below is a word, followed by three sentences which consist of that word. Identify the sentence(s) which best express(es) the meaning of the word. Choose option 5 (None of the above) if the word is not suitable in any of the sentences.

ALTRUISTIC

A. She is the most altruistic girl that I have ever come across who is so concerned excessively with oneself.

B. Rajesh is 58 so he will be altruistic from his job in two years' time.

C. Animals can have more altruistic behavior than humans.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Only C.

Key Points

  • The meaning of the word Altruistic is showing a disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others; unselfish. It is an adjective.
  • Sentence A has incorrectly used the word 'Altruistic'. Instead of altruistic the correct word should have been Selfish. Because in the latter part of the sentence it is given 'who is so concerned excessively with oneself.' 
  • The meaning of selfish is- one who is so concerned excessively with oneself.
  • Sentence B has incorrectly used the word 'Altruistic'. Instead retiring will be a suitable word.
  • As the sentence says that "Rajesh is 58 so he will be retiring from his job in two years' time."
  • Sentence C has correctly used the given word. Here it means that animals be more loving and selfless than humans.

Additional Information

Synonyms of 'Altruistic' are: philanthropic, humanitarian, selfless. 

Antonyms of 'Altruistic' are: Selfish.

questions.text:

B. Above all, try to be sacrilegious and cautious with the old prince.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Both A and C.'

Key Points

  •  The meaning of the word 'Sacrilegious' is involving or committing sacrilege; impious, sinful, irreverent, irreligious, unholy, disrespectful.
  • Sentence A has correctly used the given word. Here, it means that churches were sacked and disrespectful acts were committed.
  • In sentence B, 'sacrilegious is incorrectly used. Here, the sentence is talking to behave and give respect to the old prince. Instead, it will replaced by the word 'Respectful'. The corrected sentence will be "Above all, try to be respectful and cautious with the old prince."
  • Sentence C has correctly used the given word. Here, it means the clerics abandoned, destroyed, the book which is a disrespectful attack on their faith.

Additional Information

  • Synonyms of 'Sacrilegious'- profane, blasphemous, impious, sinful, irreligious.
  • Antonyms of 'Sacrilegious'-  pious, respectful.

questions.text:
Read the sentence given below to find out if it contains an error. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. if the sentence is error free, select No error or option 5. Ignore errors of punctuation if any.

He's living (A) with luxury (B) in the south (C) of France. (D) No Error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'B' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • The error lies in Part B of the sentence. 
  • Use 'in' in place of 'with'.
  • In - used to indicate inclusion within something abstract or immaterial.
    • Ex: He was sitting alone in the darkness.
  • With- We use with to refer to what we use to do something.
    • Ex: They opened the package with a knife.
  • Therefore, by understanding the usage of the above preposition it is clear that 'in' is the correct answer.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 2.
     

The correct sentence is: He's living in luxury in the south of France.

questions.text:
Read the sentence given below to find out if it contains an error. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. if the sentence is error free, select No error or option 5. Ignore errors of punctuation if any.

I always play (A) cricket in the (B) morning. But last (C) morning I play baseball. (D) No Error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'D' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • Replace play with played in part D.
  • The keyword Last morning indicates that the sentence is in the simple past tense.
  • The sentence structure of simple past tense is subject+ v2+ object.
    • Ex: He won the silver medal. 
  • Here, the second form of the verb Play is Played.
  • Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.
    ​

The correct sentence: I always play cricket in the morning. But last morning I played baseball.
 Important Points

  • We use the simple past tense to refer to a definite time in the past (when we specify the time or how long) and usually with past time expressions such as yesterday, two weeks ago, last year, in 1995.
  • For Examples:-
    • We met in January 1975.
    • We went to America together in 1978

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Outburst.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence "Kerala Governor Arif Mohammad Khan’s ___(1)___ against the ruling Communist Party of India (Marxist) and its functionaries including Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan marks an escalation in tensions between him and the elected government'' is talking about Kerala Governor’s strong feeling of anger against the ruling Communist Party of India (Marxist).
  • Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is 'Outburst'.
  • Also, the use of the word ''tensions'' in the sentence indicates the use of the word 'outburst' in the blank.
  • The word 'Outburst' means A sudden expression of a strong feeling, especially anger.
    • Example: She apologized for her outburst.
       

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Complete Sentence: Kerala Governor Arif Mohammad Khan’s outburst against the ruling Communist Party of India (Marxist) and its functionaries including Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan marks an escalation in tensions between him and the elected government.

Additional Information

  • Let us explore  the other options:
    • Worst means Of the poorest quality or the lowest standard; least good or desirable.
    • Thirst means A strong desire for something.
    • Assert means To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.
    • Revert means To return to a previous state, practice, topic, etc.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Despite.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence "Until now, Mr. Khan and Mr. Vijayan had maintained a functional relationship ___(2)___ their apparent differences'' is saying that Mr. Khan and Mr. Vijayan had maintained a functional relationship without being affected by their apparent differences.
  • Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is 'Despite'.
  • Also, the use of the word ''differences'' in the sentence indicates the use of the word 'despite' in the blank.
  • The word 'Despite' means Without being affected by; in spite of.
    • Example: Despite the criticisms, she remained defiant.
       

Hence, the correct answer is option 5.

Complete Sentence: Until now, Mr. Khan and Mr. Vijayan had maintained a functional relationship despite their apparent differences.

Additional Information

  • Let us explore  the other options:
    • Respite means A short period of rest or relief from something difficult or unpleasant.
    • Excite means To cause someone to feel very enthusiastic and eager.
    • Petite means Attractively small and dainty.
    • Delight means Great pleasure.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Appoint.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence "At the heart of the current flare-up is Kannur University’s controversial decision to ___(3)___ the wife of Mr. Vijayan’s private secretary as an associate professor'' is talking about designating the wife of Mr. Vijayan’s private secretary as an associate professor.
  • Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is 'Appoint'.
  • Also, the use of the word ''decision'' in the sentence indicates the use of the word 'appoint' in the blank.
  • The word 'Appoint' means To assign a job or role to someone.
    • Example: The decision to appoint Rahul was almost unanimous.
       

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Complete Sentence: At the heart of the current flare-up is Kannur University’s controversial decision to appoint the wife of Mr. Vijayan’s private secretary as an associate professor.

Additional Information

  • Let us explore  the other options:
    • Disappoint means To fail to fulfill the hopes or expectations.
    • Constraint means A limitation or restriction.
    • Complaint means A reason for dissatisfaction.
    • Point means To to aim something in the direction of somebody or something.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Critical.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence "Mr. Khan, who is also the chancellor of the university, has been ___(4)___ of the move, but his decision to hold a full-length press conference crossed a line and damaged the majesty of his office'' is talking about Mr. Khan condemning or disapproving the move of appointing Mr. Vijayan’s private secretary as an associate professor.
  • Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is 'Critical'.
  • Also, the use of the word ''move'' in the sentence indicates the use of the word 'critical' in the blank.
  • The word 'Critical' means Expressing adverse or disapproving comments or judgments.
    • Example: She became openly critical of party policy.
       

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Complete Sentence: Mr. Khan, who is also the chancellor of the university, has been critical of the move, but his decision to hold a full-length press conference crossed a line and damaged the majesty of his office.

Additional Information

  • Let us explore  the other options:
    • Economical means Giving good value or return in relation to the money, time, or effort expended.
    • Reciprocal means Given, felt, or done in return.
    • Rhetorical means Expressed in terms intended to persuade or impress.
    • Logical means Characterized by or capable of clear, sound reasoning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Labeled.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence "In the presser, Mr. Khan lashed out at CPI(M) functionaries and ___(5)___ some of their actions as being anti-national, nepotism, and anti-social'' is saying that Mr. Khan categorized or described some of the actions of CPI(M) functionaries as being anti-national, nepotism, and anti-social.
  • Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is 'Labeled'.
  • Also, the use of the word ''actions'' in the sentence indicates the use of the word 'labeled' in the blank.
  • The word 'Labeled' means To describe somebody or something in a particular way, especially unfairly.

Roger Federer and Serena Williams, both of whom will turn 40 in 2021, have already players (A) to allowed (B) in Australia but the committed (C) simply will not show up if they are not playing (D) to prepare (E) properly.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is CDABE.

Important Points

Let us consider A, B, C, D, and E to be five blanks, with A being the first, B the second, and so on.
  • The first blank requires a past participle as it is preceded by the verb 'have'. Thus, the correct answer is 'committed'. 
  • The second blank requires a verb in the present continuous tense and 'allowed' is in the past tense, thus the correct answer is 'playing'. 
  • The third blank requires a noun, as a verb is not an entity that can 'show up'. Thus, the correct answer is 'players'. 
  • The fourth blank requires a verb in the past tense, thus the correct answer is 'allowed'. 
  • The fifth blank requires a verb in the present tense, thus the correct answer is 'prepare'. 'To' is usually followed by the base form of the verb.

Additional Information

Let's look at the meaning of the words:

  • Committed: Past tense of 'commit', which means to be dedicated to something, to agree to do something. 
  • Playing: Present continuous tense of 'play', which means to take part in a sport. 
  • Players: Plural of 'player', which is a person who is taking part in a sport or a game.
  • Allowed: Past tense of 'allow', which means to give permission to someone; agreeing to let them do something.
  • Prepare: Make something ready for use; to become ready to perform. 
     

Thus, the correct sentence: Roger Federer and Serena Williams, both of whom will turn 40 in 2021, have already committed to playing in Australia but the players simply will not show up if they are not allowed to prepare properly.

  • Destroyed: Ruined or damaged something.

  • The second blank requires a noun that the preceding label 'Boeing 777' is a category of, and 'Boeing 777' is a type of aircraft and so 'aircrafts' is the correct answer. 
  • The third blank requires a verb in the past tense and thus an adjective like 'second' needs to be replaced with the verb 'modified'. 
  • The fourth blank requires a noun and 'arrive' is a verb, thus the correct answer is 'travel'. 
  • The fifth blank requires a verb in the present tense (infinitive form) and one cannot 'travel in' a location, one can 'travel to' a location, thus the correct answer is 'arrive'. 

Additional Information  

Let' look at the meaning of all the words:

  • Modified: Past tense of 'modify' which means to make changes to or in. 
  • Travel: The act of travelling. 
  • Arrive: To reach the place at the end of a journey; the final stage of a journey. 

Thus, the correct sentence will be: The second of the two Boeing 777 aircrafts extensively modified for the President, the Vice President and Prime Minister’s travel will arrive in national capital Delhi on Saturday.
